title: Agent-proposed vortex scale improves a reference-flow prediction
summary: Claude-driven agents translated a human-supplied vortex-axis modeling idea into candidate subgrid length scales. The selected Liutex-based formulation predicted backward-step reattachment at 7.13 step heights versus the published experimental 6.67; the standard scale predicted 12.50. This is a selected computational closure result, not a new experimentally observed turbulence mechanism.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 5.5 discovery, review, implementation and evaluation agents
organization: Iowa State University; Pennsylvania State University

evidence.tested: Candidate formulas were screened sequentially on four canonical/engineering flows using published references. The selected closure was similar to, or slightly better than, an expert shear-layer-adapted baseline.
evidence.unknown: The same cases drove selection, not an untouched validation suite. Five runs repeated proposal/review/implementation but did not repeat expensive flow simulations. Human concept, reference data and fallback assumptions constrain discovery. No universal closure superiority or real-aircraft benefit is established.
evidence.ai_role: LLM agents derived and implemented explicit vortex-axis-based formulas rather than merely executing a fully specified human closure. Subsequent numerical solvers evaluated their physical predictions.

source_review.scope: Actual primary candidate-generation Methods, selection workflow, reference-flow Results/Table6 and physical fallback interpretation; current v1 date/status.
